_about: Changes that alter how agents behave. A new install starts with each one on. An install that already has agents gets each new entry switched off and waiting for its owner's decision: its lead agent reviews the change for that install and explains it, and the owner turns it on or leaves it off on the /changes page. Add an entry here for any future change to agent behaviour; never switch one on for existing installs by itself.

changes.title: Team advice in agents' instructions
changes.changes: Adds a short "running a team" section to agents' instructions: when to do a job themselves and when to hand it to a worker, which kind of model suits which job, how to write a brief, and how to get a second opinion and an adversarial check from a different model. Lead agents get the full version, other agents a core version, small local models and members' agents a short one. Turning it on gives it to the lead and to agents created from then on; agents that already exist get it only when it is switched on for them one by one (agent settings, Team guidance).
changes.benefits: Agents that hand out work do it more often and better: cheaper models for routine work, the strongest model kept for planning and hard reviews, important work checked by a second model before it is relied on.
changes.costs: About 450 words more in each lead turn's instructions (about 120 for the short version), and some extra worker or reviewer runs where an agent decides a job needs them.
changes.check: Which agents here already hand out work (consult_agent, spawn_workers) and how; whether their own instructions already cover delegation; which agents would benefit most (usually the primary agents that do long or many-part jobs).
changes.on: The lead and new agents get it; existing agents when switched on one by one.

changes.title: A starter team: a Challenger and three workers
changes.changes: Offers to create four agents: a Challenger that reviews important work adversarially, Scout for lookups and summaries, Builder for coding and multi-step work, Researcher for research and writing. They use cheaper models on the plans this install already pays for; the Challenger uses another company's model where one is connected. Turning it on shows a Set up your team card; nothing is created until the owner presses Create there. An agent name that is already taken is skipped.
changes.benefits: The lead has ready workers to hand routine work to and a second model to check important work, without setting them up by hand.
changes.costs: Each agent uses its model when it is given work; one billed per use is marked on the card before anything is created.
changes.check: Whether agents with these roles already exist here (a reviewer, a quick helper, a coder, a researcher), which models the workers would get, and whether any would be billed per use.
changes.on: The Set up your team card appears for an admin; agents are created only from it.
changes.off: No card and no starter agents.

changes.title: Members' temporary workers use only the models members may choose
changes.changes: A family member's agent can start temporary workers (spawn_workers). With this on, those workers may run only on that agent's own model and the models the admin lets members choose for their own agents (the members' model list); any other model is refused. (The member limits on reasoning and speed apply to their workers either way.) With it off, a member's temporary workers may use any model this install reaches, as before.
changes.benefits: Members can't spend the owner's money on models the admin didn't allow them, for example a top model billed per use.
changes.costs: A member's agent that relied on a model outside the list for its workers gets a refusal naming the allowed models; the admin may need to add a model to the members' list.
changes.check: Whether this install has members, which models their agents use, what the members' model list holds, and whether members' agents start temporary workers today.
changes.on: Members' temporary workers are limited to the agent's own model and the members' model list.
changes.off: Members' temporary workers may use any reachable model.

changes.title: The lead suggests new workers from how the install is used
changes.changes: Once a week the lead looks at a summary of how agents were used in the past seven days (requests per agent and model, errors, temporary workers it keeps starting) and, when a pattern would be better served by a permanent worker or specialist, proposes one to the owner in plain words: its name, job, model and what it would save or improve. At most one short proposal at a time; it builds one only on the owner's yes. For members' agents it uses counts only, never their conversations.
changes.benefits: Repeated work moves to the right agent and model over time instead of the lead redoing it, or a top model spending itself on routine jobs.
changes.costs: One short lead turn a week; occasionally a proposal to read.
changes.check: How busy this install is, whether the owner wants suggestions, and which agents do repeated work on expensive models.
changes.on: A weekly look and at most one proposal at a time (Settings: Worker proposals, weekly or off).
changes.off: No weekly look and no proposals.

changes.title: Primary agents ask the lead for workers they need
changes.changes: Adds one line to primary agents' instructions: when they need a worker or a specialist they don't have, they ask the lead (by name) with the job, a proposed name and the model tier they think it needs; the lead decides with the owner. A member's main agent asks through its existing request to an admin instead, and a member's other agents ask that member's main agent; they never reach the admin's agents.
changes.benefits: Gaps in the team surface to the lead and the owner instead of an agent struggling on its own.
changes.costs: Now and then a request for the lead to answer.
changes.check: Which primary agents exist here and whether the lead should hear from them.
